title: Sanskrit Wikisource's texts released as a single IAST download
dek: A Brazilian scholar has converted every Devanagari text on Sanskrit Wikisource to IAST and gathered them into 2,653 works in one 135 MB file. The conversion was done by script, so the texts are only as reliable as the Wikisource pages behind them.
body: The texts of Sanskrit Wikisource (sa.wikisource.org) can now be downloaded as one compressed file of plain-text works in IAST, the standard Roman transliteration for Sanskrit. The collection was made by Roberto de Andrade Martins, who describes himself as a Brazilian scholar, and was uploaded to the Internet Archive on 16 November 2026. Harry Spier forwarded his announcement to the INDOLOGY mailing list on 19 November.

According to the Internet Archive record, the source was the official Wikimedia XML dumps of Sanskrit Wikisource. Martins says he took all 23,872 Devanagari files on the site as of mid-November 2026, converted them to IAST and joined the separate parts of each work into a single text file. The result is 2,653 works and, by the record's count, about 39.8 million words, in UTF-8 text.

The archive, a RAR file of about 135 MB, also holds a spreadsheet catalogue of every work, and a set of the six largest works split into volumes of under 280,000 words each. Martins's announcement also links a GitHub repository, but when we checked on 20 November it held only a short description and not the archive itself.

The record says the processing scripts were written by Gemini, Google's AI assistant, working with Martins, and that the transliteration was done with the indic-transliteration software. Neither the record nor the announcement says that the texts were checked by hand after conversion, so they carry over any errors in the Wikisource pages or the conversion. Anyone quoting a passage should check it against a printed edition.

The record says the original texts are in the public domain, while the transcriptions and the compilation are under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 licence, so derived collections must use the same licence and credit Sanskrit Wikisource. Questions go to Martins, whose address is given on the record and in the list post.
